rationale: Across all available literature and clinical databases describing Popov-Chang syndrome (POPCHAS; OMIM #618428) caused by pathogenic variation in YWHAZ, global developmental delay/intellectual disability (HP:0001263 / HP:0001249) and speech/language impairment or delay (HP:0000750) are consistently documented across 100% of described affected individuals. No documented counter-examples of non-penetrance or individuals with preserved speech and normal intellectual development were identified in the reported cohorts.

evidence.text: Popov-Chang syndrome is defined as an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by global developmental delay, impaired intellectual development, and poor or absent speech.

evidence.text: In a large multi-generational pedigree, a novel missense variant in YWHAZ (c.147A>T, p.Lys49Asn) segregated with intellectual disability, global developmental delay, and speech development delay in all affected family members.

new_directions.question_text: What specific dysmorphic features or neuroimaging signatures reliably distinguish Popov-Chang syndrome from other 14-3-3 proteinopathies or general intellectual disability syndromes?
new_directions.rationale: Because global developmental delay and speech impairment are generic neurodevelopmental phenotypes with high background frequency across hundreds of genetic conditions, identifying unique dysmorphology or brain MRI findings is essential for syndromic delineation.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true penetrance and expressivity spectrum of YWHAZ loss-of-function versus gain-of-function/dominant-negative variants across unselected biobank exome cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Ascertainment bias in early family pedigrees and targeted cohorts often overestimates the penetrance of severe cognitive phenotypes; searching population databases (e.g., gnomAD, UK Biobank) will test whether mild or non-penetrant alleles exist.
